label: Compactness: The Chapter Question
notes: Chapter four spans printed pages seventy-five through one hundred fourteen and asks what becomes of a bounded-energy sequence of J-holomorphic curves. The answer is Gromov compactness: no smooth limit in general, but a cusp curve obtained after extracting bubbles, with energy conserved throughout the process.

label: Energy of a J-holomorphic Curve
notes: Energy is the central currency of the chapter. For a J-holomorphic map it equals the symplectic area, so a uniform energy bound is geometric, not analytic. This identity is why bounded energy forces the strong conclusions of compactness rather than merely controlling some abstract norm.

label: Gromov Compactness Theorem
notes: Gromov's theorem is the destination. A sequence with a common energy bound has a subsequence converging modulo reparametrization to a cusp curve. Convergence is uniform away from finitely many bubble points, and at those points the geometry resolves into attached spheres carrying the missing energy.

label: Bubbling: Energy Concentration
notes: Bubbling is the obstruction to naive convergence. Where the derivative blows up, energy piles into a vanishing disk and cannot pass to the limit smoothly. The notebook heatmap models this with a broad base component and two sharply localized bubbles, each integrating to a definite positive energy.

label: Rescaling Extracts a Sphere
notes: Rescaling is the rescue. Zooming the coordinate around a concentration point at the rate the gradient blows up produces a new finite-energy J-holomorphic map on the plane. The notebook's rescaling chart shows bubble energy staying fixed while the visible radius grows as the chart magnifies the neighborhood.

label: Removal of Singularities
notes: Removal of singularities closes the construction. A J-holomorphic map on a punctured disk with finite energy extends smoothly across the puncture. Applied to the rescaled plane this fills the point at infinity, turning the limit into a genuine sphere rather than a map with a hole in it.

label: The Mean-Value Inequality
notes: The mean-value inequality is the local engine. It converts small energy on a disk into a pointwise bound on the derivative at the center. The notebook ledger checks that each observed derivative peak sits below its computed mean-value bound, the quantitative reason small energy means smooth control.

label: The Isoperimetric Inequality
notes: The isoperimetric inequality controls boundary loops: a short loop bounds little area in the symplectic sense. The notebook records the Euclidean ratio L squared over four pi A equal to one for circular models. This loop estimate is the boundary tool that drives the removal of singularities argument.

label: The Energy Quantum: No Energy Loss
notes: Monotonicity yields a minimal energy quantum: every nonconstant bubble carries at least hbar units of energy. With a finite total budget only finitely many bubbles can form, and no energy leaks into infinitely many invisible pieces. The threshold separates a genuine bubble from a harmless sharp peak.

label: The Bubble Tree Limit
notes: The components assemble into a bubble tree. A principal curve carries sphere bubbles at its nodes, and Chapter four point seven proves this graph is connected and acyclic. The notebook draws this tree with energy labels, the connected structure that becomes the stable map of the next chapter.

label: Energy Accounting Across the Limit
notes: The accounting is exact: total energy of the limit equals the original bound, split between the principal curve and the bubbles. The notebook checks conservation to numerical zero. This balance, not any single estimate, is the heart of why bounded energy yields a compact limit object.

label: Proof Architecture and Takeaways
notes: The proof flow is recognizable: energy bounds locate concentration, mean-value control gives smooth convergence elsewhere, isoperimetric control removes singularities, rescaling extracts bubbles, quantization gives finiteness, and connectedness builds the tree. Track where energy concentrates, what scale reveals a bubble, how much it carries, and how components attach.
